headline: SUNDAY CREEK LINKS TWO GOLD ZONES ACROSS 481m — 0.8m @ 141 g/t Au Peak Proves High-Grade System Extends 1,000m Below Surface; Westernmost Hole Opens New Corridor (ASX: SX2 / TSX: SXGC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Southern Cross Gold
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (ASX: SX2 / TSX: SXGC) reported July 28 that its westernmost and deepest hole at the Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria intersected 481 metres of continuous mineralisation linking the Christina Prospect directly into the Golden Dyke corridor — a geological connection previously undrilled — including a peak intersection of 0.8 metres at 141.0 g/t gold and individual assays reaching 496 g/t gold. The hole remained within prospective host rock for a cumulative 800 metres of its 1,405-metre total depth, defining productive mineralisation 1,000 metres below surface at the project's far western margin. With 11 rigs turning on a 200,000-metre program through Q1 2027 and 68 holes currently awaiting assays, Sunday Creek continues to expand both laterally and at depth.

headline: CHINA'S NDRC STALLS $4B ZIJIN GOLD TAKEOVER — July 29 Outside Date Passes Without Closure; Allied Gold Parties Expected to Extend to October 31 as Regulator Scrutinizes Premium (TSX: AAUC)
snippet: Zijin Gold International's C$44/share takeover of Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AAUC) missed its July 29, 2026 outside date without closing after China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) escalated the deal to in-depth review, questioning the premium paid in a transaction that hands a Chinese state-linked entity control over Allied's five producing gold mines in Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, and Ethiopia. Every other regulator — Canada, the United States, the EU, ECOWAS, and COMESA — has signed off; NDRC is the sole remaining hurdle, making this effectively a bilateral diplomatic friction point dressed as a merger review. The parties are expected to extend the long-stop date to October 31, 2026, the third extension since the arrangement was announced in January 2026.

headline: BANYAN GOLD HITS 17.80 g/t Au IN FIRST NITRA HOLES — Two New Zones Discovered 25km West of AurMac; Roaring Fork + Seattle Creek Greenfields Success Opens Royalty-Free District (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) reported July 28 the inaugural results from its helicopter-supported diamond drill program at the Nitra Project in Yukon — 25 kilometres west of its 10.1-million-ounce AurMac Deposit — with opening hole NT-26-001 at the newly identified Roaring Fork Zone returning 1.62 g/t gold over 5.0 metres, including 17.80 g/t gold over 0.4 metres. A second target, the Seattle Creek Zone, returned visible gold in core from first contact. Both Nitra discoveries sit on ground owned 100% by Banyan with no underlying royalties, giving the company unencumbered leverage on a new district play just as AurMac advances toward a PEA with leading mining consultants engaged.

headline: MOCOA DRILLS 584m @ 0.73% CuEq AND BEATS 2026 RESOURCE MODEL — Third Corridor Continuous at Depth Ahead of PEA; Colombia's Largest Undeveloped Copper System Gets Wider (TSXV: CGNT)
source_name: Skillings Mining Review / Copper Giant Resources
snippet: Copper Giant Resources Corp. (TSXV: CGNT) reported July 28 that infill hole MD-066 at its Mocoa copper-molybdenum porphyry project in Putumayo, Colombia, returned 584 metres of continuous mineralisation at 0.73% CuEq (0.40% Cu, 0.062% Mo) — grades that exceed the existing Mocoa Resource Model and extend the high-grade envelope at depth ahead of a PEA expected later in 2026. Companion corridor hole MD-065 further extended the newly confirmed third mineralised corridor along strike, strengthening the geometry of a system that is one of the largest undeveloped copper porphyries in South America at a time when Citi holds a year-end copper price target of $15,000/t.

headline: INAUGURAL COPALITO DRILL: 675 g/t AgEq IN 0.80m AT EL PILAR VEIN — First Hole Exceeds Pre-Drill Expectations; Sinaloa Silver-Gold Vein System Just Getting Started (CSE: MERC)
snippet: Mercado Minerals Ltd. (CSE: MERC) reported July 28 the opening results of its 3,000-metre inaugural diamond drill program at the Copalito Project in Sinaloa, Mexico, with the El Pilar Vein delivering 0.80 metres of 675 g/t silver equivalent (9 g/t Ag, 5.37 g/t Au, 1.65% Pb, 10.05% Zn) within a broader 3.40-metre interval averaging 403 g/t AgEq — the highest silver-equivalent grade recorded at the project to date. The intersection demonstrates that high-grade polymetallic veins are present at drillable depths, with the bulk of the 3,000-metre program still to test strike and depth extensions of a vein system that has had significant surface expressions but minimal prior drilling.

headline: DRILL RIG ARRIVES AT SHIRLEY CENTRAL, WYOMING — Noble Plains Converts 341 Historical Uranium Intercepts Into Live Confirmation Program Adjacent to Ur-Energy's ISR Mine (TSXV: NOBL)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Noble Plains Uranium
snippet: Noble Plains Uranium Corp. (TSXV: NOBL) announced July 28 that a drill rig has been mobilized to its Shirley Central Project in Wyoming's Shirley Basin and that a confirmation drill program has commenced — the specific objective being to convert 341 qualifying historical uranium intercepts in documented roll-front clusters toward a NI 43-101-compliant mineral resource estimate. The project sits on 30 unpatented mineral claims covering 665 acres adjacent to the boundary of Ur-Energy's operating Shirley Basin in-situ recovery uranium mine. Noble Plains completed digitisation of over 1,200 historical drill holes earlier this month, identifying the qualifying intercepts at an estimated replacement cost exceeding US$6 million in new drilling.

headline: CME'S 24/7 GOLD FUTURES DEBUT LOGS $60M FIRST WEEKEND — Spreads Hit $0.25; Around-the-Clock Gold Trading Meets Global Retail Demand Without a Close for the First Time
snippet: CME Group's 1-ounce gold futures contract began continuous 24/7 trading on July 26, 2026, with the inaugural weekend logging approximately 15,000 contracts — roughly $60 million in notional value — and bid-ask spreads tightening to as little as $0.25 at peak activity. The launch eliminates the daily market close that has historically allowed off-hours price dislocation, letting retail and institutional participants trade gold around the clock in a regulated futures environment for the first time. The 1-ounce contract format, which averaged 87,000 lots of daily volume in the first half of 2026, is designed to lower the capital barrier for smaller participants seeking precise gold exposure without ETF basis risk.

headline: NdPr ALLOY +21% TO $133/kg IN JULY — NEW 2026 HIGH AS SECOND CONSECUTIVE SUPPLY DEFICIT WIDENS; EV and Wind Demand Outpacing Chinese Quota Expansion, Heavy Rare Earths Also Scarce
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium alloy prices surged approximately 21% in July 2026 to around $133/kg — the highest monthly benchmark of the year, clearing the previous March peak — as the NdPr market enters its second consecutive year of structural supply deficit with EV and wind-turbine demand outpacing both Chinese quota expansions and the ramp-up of Western production capacity. Neodymium and praseodymium metals rose nearly 20% each in tandem; China's rare earth producer index remains elevated while heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) show separate scarcity signals as state stockpile managers restrict below-quota availability. Permanent-magnet input costs are now tracking roughly 40% above mid-2025 lows, squeezing EV motor manufacturers that failed to lock in long-term contracts.

headline: GOLD FELL. THE CASE IS INTACT — Post-FOMC Analysis: $4,000 Floor Holds Through Six Rate-Decision Tests; Warsh Hawkishness Is a Shrinking Window, Not a New Trend
snippet: GoldSilver.com's post-FOMC July 2026 analysis argues that gold's price decline following the Fed's hold does not invalidate the structural bull case — the $4,000 level has now served as defended support through six consecutive FOMC rate-decision periods without a confirmed daily close below it, and Chair Warsh's hawkish framing represents a narrowing window of upside rate risk as inflation data continues to trend lower. The piece identifies Q3 2026 as a historically strong seasonal window for gold and notes that current positioning is compressed enough that a soft June PCE print (due Thursday) could trigger a sharp reversal from a technically oversold baseline that looks very different from the January $5,595 peak.
